solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Publication by students with classy, clean content, fantastic achievement

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication

indicators.note: content here means contents, so the students hold the next pieces inside them

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
U means upper-class, hence classy
to mop is to clean

explanation.surface: A student magazine with tidy, respectable articles hailed as a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classy' for U is the old upper-class label, as in U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for a great work names an artist's or writer's finest achievement.

clue.text: Be getting on motorway over part of England to make fortune

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the pair is flipped bottom to top

parts.note: to age is to be getting on in years
M is a motorway, as in the M1
Bucks is Buckinghamshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Getting old on the motorway across the shires to make your money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a huge amount of money, a fortune.

clue.text: Smile, darling, although missing a tooth

parts.note: a grin is a smile

indicators.note: missing says the letter a is lost from the darling word

parts.note: dear is a term for a darling

explanation.surface: A sweetheart's grin with a gap where a tooth should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Molars are back teeth that crush food; such a tooth is called by this name.

clue.text: To take a rich husband, they say, may be a bloomer

indicators.note: they say signals that the words heard are spelt differently

parts.note: to wed money is to marry gold

explanation.surface: Wedding for money is a big mistake, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' means a blunder on the surface but a flowering plant here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a plant in flower, and this orange garden flower is one.

clue.text: Pay attention: after nip, as it were, I burn

parts.note: nip written backwards spells pin, so pin back describes it
I is one, as a pronoun
to sear is to burn

explanation.surface: Listen up: after a cold nip, I start to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to listen carefully, ears pulled back to catch every word.

clue.text: Worked out divided county has ended up different

indicators.note: the final letter of the county is changed for another

parts.note: Sussex is an English county split into East and West Sussex

explanation.surface: A split county turned out quite different.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the new last letter; the definition and crossings give D.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for figured out or understood is this word.

clue.text: Youngster swallows large part of tooth

indicators.note: the youngster takes the next letter down inside itself

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, a youngster
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A puppy gulps down a big piece of a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft inner tissue of a tooth, holding nerves and blood vessels, carries this name.

clue.text: Lying for the country has caught ambassador finally

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the country holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a state is a country

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador finally caught telling lies for his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' means lying flat, not telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying face down, flat on the ground, is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Saying little boy almost in shape for ice cream?

indicators.note: almost cuts the last letter from the boy word

parts.note: a lad is a boy
cone-shaped, like an ice-cream cone

explanation.surface: A quiet little boy shaped like an ice-cream cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse person who uses few words is described as such.

clue.text: Where some are playing football, or riding around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the words or riding are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A field where people play football or ride horses.
explanation.definitionFit: American football is played on a field marked like a grill, which gives the field its nickname.

clue.text: Lights finally low, central heating on, kiss and cuddle

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word Lights

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
CH is the estate-agent abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: Lights down, heating on, a couple settle in for a romantic evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle closely with kissing is exactly this, a slangy word for necking.

clue.text: Corpse is gory: look out

indicators.note: out says the following word's letters are taken away from the synonym

parts.note: gory means bloody
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A crime-scene warning: the dead man is a grisly sight, so look away.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead person's remains are routinely called a body by police and pathologists.

clue.text: A reminder of the late quality of wine

indicators.note: quality of wine puts the wine first and the quality after it

parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux wine region and its wine
tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: A wine's character keeps the memory of a lost friend alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone over a burial place keeps the dead in mind, a memorial to the departed.

clue.text: Scrub fork clean for a bit of breakfast

indicators.note: scrub as slang for cancel or scrap tells us to break up the words fork clean and rebuild them

explanation.surface: Wash the cutlery after breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: One flake of a popular breakfast cereal is a small piece of the morning meal.

clue.text: See blonde squirming: why is she red in the face?

definitions.text: why is she red in the face?

indicators.note: squirming suggests the letters of see blonde wriggle into another order

explanation.surface: Watch a blonde woman writhing with embarrassment; why is she blushing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'red in the face' suggests a blush, but the redness is blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleeding from the nostrils would leave someone's face red with blood.

clue.text: Refuse hard slog

parts.note: marc is the refuse of grapes after pressing
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone declines a tough trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tiring walk, a trek or tramp, is a slog.

clue.text: Hotel inside western city a mile and six feet

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: inside says the next pieces go into the city

parts.note: Exeter is a city in south-west England

explanation.surface: A hotel in a West Country city a mile away, six feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six feet' means six metrical feet, not a height.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse line of six metrical feet is described by this word.

clue.text: Portrait of animal so original

indicators.note: original suggests the letters of animal so are made into something new

explanation.surface: A painting of a creature, quite unique.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's famous painting in the Louvre is a portrait of a smiling woman.

clue.text: Burned remains after emptying secret store

indicators.note: after places the remains following the emptied word
emptying the word secret removes its inside letters, leaving only its two ends

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Ashes scattered after someone clears out a hidden hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secret store' looks like the definition, but 'secret' supplies ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden supply or reserve put by is a hoard, which is a store.

clue.text: Speak badly of drug, taken regularly in tiny amount

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the tiny amount

parts.note: a trace is a tiny amount

indicators.note: taken regularly picks every other letter of the word drug

explanation.surface: Slander someone over a drug taken regularly in small doses.
explanation.definitionFit: To defame or malign someone is to speak ill of them.

clue.text: Loss of earnings shocking to Mexican

indicators.note: shocking hints the letters of to Mexican are jolted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A Mexican worker is appalled at how much pay is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax taken from wages reduces take-home pay, so it is a loss of money earned.

clue.text: Composer reaching height? Rather unlikely

indicators.note: reaching places the height letter after the composer

parts.note: Thomas Tallis was an English Tudor composer

explanation.surface: A composer's career reaching great heights seems improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: A tall story is an unlikely one, so 'rather tall' is rather unlikely.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall in the sense of hard to believe, as in a tall tale; somewhat so is rather unlikely.

clue.text: Palladium, introducing old character, cut back

indicators.note: the element takes the old letter into its middle

parts.note: Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium
a rune is a letter of an old alphabet

explanation.surface: The Palladium theatre brings back an old character but cuts the show.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim branches or costs is to reduce or cut them back.

clue.text: Two obstacles, very large: it's for a Russian invasion

indicators.note: two signals the obstacle word is given twice

parts.note: a bar is an obstacle
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Huge barriers set up to stop a Russian attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation Barbarossa was the codename for Germany's 1941 attack on the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Creed not one to criticise harshly

indicators.note: not one says the letter standing for one is dropped

parts.note: Islam is a religious creed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A faith that refuses to condemn anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics who savage a play are said to pan or lambast it, a harsh attack.

clue.text: Dish youngster eats sport being over

indicators.note: the youngster takes the sport inside it

parts.note: a teen is a youngster

indicators.note: over signals the sport letters are turned back to front

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A teenager eats a meal after the match has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being over' looks like the match ending, but it turns the sport around.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep covered bowl for serving soup is a serving dish.

clue.text: A chronicler's first to be replaced — his charges can be stinging

indicators.note: the opening letter of the chronicler word is swapped for another

parts.note: a diarist chronicles daily events

explanation.surface: A historian is sacked and his clients are angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces D; P is found from the definition and crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper's charges are bees, which can sting.

clue.text: Caught, not many would quarrel at length

indicators.note: caught as in heard, so the words are what the ear picks up

parts.note: few'd is not many would, contracted

explanation.surface: Seized, hardly anyone would argue for long.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running bitter dispute is a quarrel that drags on.

clue.text: Router sends digger round Bath

indicators.note: the digger goes around the spa town

parts.note: a ditcher digs ditches
Bath is a spa town in Somerset

explanation.surface: A network router forwards traffic, while a labourer works around Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Router' is not network kit but one who routes, as a dispatcher sends things out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sends vehicles or goods on their way directs their route.
